subject: Problem: Plotting by numeric order instead of factor order

messages.author: bb527a4a50003ee0
messages.subject: Problem: Plotting by numeric order instead of factor order
parts:
I am using factored/ordered data, and ggplot seems to be ignoring the factor order, and instead following the continuous/numeric data order.  I have attached a jpeg of an ouput plot, this ordering makes it really difficult to interpret the data, and I am sure I am missing something small.  How do I get this to plot by factor correctly?

below is a subset of data, and attached is subset plotted

Data
          time           treatment    variable    value
4   08/25/09:N Ambient CO2 Control  X10cm.mean 36.39274
16  08/25/09:N Ambient CO2 Control  X20cm.mean 40.36536
28  08/25/09:N Ambient CO2 Control  X30cm.mean 42.46743
40  08/25/09:N Ambient CO2 Control  X40cm.mean 43.48431
52  08/25/09:N Ambient CO2 Control  X50cm.mean 47.00896
64  08/25/09:N Ambient CO2 Control  X60cm.mean 48.11792
76  08/25/09:N Ambient CO2 Control  X70cm.mean 47.54671
88  08/25/09:N Ambient CO2 Control  X80cm.mean 48.06299
100 08/25/09:N Ambient CO2 Control  X90cm.mean 47.04015
112 08/25/09:N Ambient CO2 Control X100cm.mean 47.50861

form$time <- ordered(form$time)
form$treatment <- factor(form$factor)
form$variable <- ordered(form$variable)
form$time <- ordered(form$time)

Data Classes
> sapply(form, data.class)
     time treatment  variable     value
"ordered"  "factor" "ordered" "numeric"

Plot Code
p <- ggplot(form, aes(x=value, y=variable, group=treatment, colour=treatment))
p + geom_line() + geom_point()

--

messages.author: bb527a4a50003ee0
messages.subject: Re: Problem: Plotting by numeric order instead of factor order
parts:
The x axis is a continuous value, labeled value.

The Y axis is a categorical orderd factor, labeled variable

the geom_line() should plot the continuous value points along the categorical value.

Where instead it is plotting the categorical variable along the continuous value.

Pat

messages.subject: Re: Problem: Plotting by numeric order instead of factor order
parts:
Hi Pat,

A line is order by the x values. If you want to order by something
different, using the path geom and the order aesthetic.

Hadley

Hi Pat, try this:

form$variables<-factor(form$variables, levels=rev(levels(form$variables)), ordered=T)

bye

Luciano

Pat
